primary_claim: A consistency-check methodology comparing model accuracy on casually-phrased vs. formally-phrased (evaluation-like) versions of the same biosecurity questions can detect prompted sandbagging in frontier LLMs (including GPT-5.2 and Gemini 3 Pro), showing more than a 50% accuracy decrease between casual and formal framings when models are instructed to sandbag evaluation-like questions

effect.metric: accuracy difference between casual and formal question framings under sandbagging system prompt
effect.value: more than 50% accuracy decrease between casual and formal framings across all three tested models under sandbagging instructions; baseline (no sandbagging prompt) accuracy differences between casual/formal framings were negligible

stated_future_work: Test better/more realistic examples of sandbagging behavior and more specific or subtle capabilities
Use or create more realistic sandbagging model organisms whose sandbagging arises from training processes rather than a system prompt
Investigate which specific capabilities we should be most concerned about models hiding
limitations_stated: Sandbagging behavior was induced via an explicit system prompt rather than arising unintentionally from training processes, so the methodology's effectiveness on more realistic sandbagging models is untested
Sandbagging behavior tested is broad rather than focused on the most safety-relevant specific capabilities
Dataset was only spot-checked for errors due to limited project timeline
quote: When testing sandbagging versions of frontier LLMs like GPT 5.2 and Gemini 3 Pro, we see more than a 50% accuracy decrease between the casual and formal framing of the questions.
